trust_decision.summary: Which Fluid ViewHelpers may execute when an editor/TypoScript-supplied email subject string is parsed as a Fluid template; decided by an allow-list ViewHelper invoker set in FluidRenderingService::parseString. At the pinned commit this protection is ALREADY present (pin is post-fix).

landing_point.why: parseString() is the only place that sets a user-influenced string as Fluid template source (line 93); the advisory summary (SSTI) points straight to it.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: unknown: the published fix commits contain no source change, so there is no site or route to argue out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Subjects must keep rendering plain variables ({registration.firstname}) plus f:format.date and f:translate, and admin-configured additionalAllowedViewHelpers; an over-broad fix (escaping or disabling Fluid) breaks these. Already implemented and tested at the pin.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a planted second subject/body-from-string parse path (e.g. backend custom-notification overwriteSubject rendered through a separate StandaloneView helper) that skips AllowedViewHelperInvoker
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: overwriteSubject is free-text from the backend notify form (Classes/Controller/AdministrationController.php:487) and a maintainer could plausibly render it with a fresh view instead of parseString.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second string-render method (e.g. for iCal description or email body snippets) that builds the rendering context without setViewHelperInvoker/NullFluidCache
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the hardening is per-call context configuration, easy to omit when a helper method is copied.
